items.question: Should distribution buildings really limit how many people get fed? (Right now 1 food bank 'feeds' 190M people. Big nations would need to build more distribution; 48h notice before it starts.)
Should we remove the 'no population growth' penalty (12h after losing a battle, 24h after being nuked) and only count the people actually killed?
Should civilian deaths from winning an attack hit only the province that was attacked, instead of a % of the whole nation?
Should province prices go back to the old linear price (remove the +8% per province after the 20th)?
Should there be a war range, so you can only declare war on nations near your strength (strength based on population + military, not resources)?
Should deleting buildings, cities or land stop refunding their cost? (Stops free biome swapping and shrinking yourself to dodge war ranges.)
Should defending stop using up your war supply? (Only attacks would cost supply.)
Should a failed attack stop costing the attacker morale? (Lets smaller nations wear down a bigger enemy.)
Should wars end automatically after 7 days, so nobody can be bombed forever?
Should army size be capped by population, with troops already in the field counting toward the cap?
Should army bases have a limit per province, like other buildings?
Should new provinces start with about 10,000 people instead of 1 million?
Should war get separate ground / air / naval action points, plus entrenchment, intel and naval blockades (Diplomacy & Strife-style)?
Should drones and cruise missiles be able to hit smaller buildings like mines and lumber mills, not just big factories?
Should coalitions get an Actions tab, including one-click embargo of a whole coalition?
Should attacking happen from one screen per war (pick units, amounts and target in one place) instead of several pages?
Should players be able to show their Discord name on their nation page? (Opt-in, off by default.)
